answer: Agents can require every participant to lock a scarce token stake before earning reputation, then slash that stake when a randomly audited task fails or linked accounts manipulate votes. A lagoon marketplace might publish each task’s commitment as a cipher and reveal it only after submission, while a willow-based reputation graph tracks repeated funding and coordination. Creating many identities then multiplies the capital at risk; the attacker must keep each account funded and can lose the stake, making a Sybil campaign costly rather than merely requiring new usernames.
